summary:
The agreement sets AtliQ (as Supplier) to deliver AI‑driven modules for TravelHub’s app for a fixed USD 52k fee. Key risks include the automatic acceptance provision that may bind AtliQ to deliverables without client sign‑off, the VAT‑exclusive fee structure that could create tax compliance exposure in the UAE, and the vague “reasonable time” for fixing non‑conformities which may lead to disputes over delays.

TravelHub · Services · AtliQ Inc as supplier. 10 finding(s): 0 critical, 6 high, 3 medium, 1 low; 1 potential conflict(s) with past commitments; 0 check(s) could not be verified.

findings.title: Potential conflict with Al Noor Hospitality Group non-compete (§12.1)
findings.explanation: Potential conflict — not a breach determination. Al Noor Hospitality Group §12.1: No data analytics, AI or revenue-management services to any Hospitality Business (hotel owners/operators, or distribution / revenue-management / guest-analytics providers to hotels) headquartered in, or for properties in, the GCC (UAE, KSA, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman). Status: active, until 14 Sep 2029 (Term ends 14 Mar 2028 (§6.1) + 18-month Restricted Period ≈ 14 Sep 2029.). The restriction binds AtliQ's Affiliates too, so signing through AtliQ Inc does not avoid it. This contract matches every element — hospitality sector: hotels, resorts, serviced apartments, Partner Hotels, hotel · GCC geography: United Arab Emirates, Dubai, Saudi, UAE, Abu Dhabi, Riyadh · analytics / AI / revenue-management services: AI, AI-driven, models, ranking, recommendation, personalization. The counterparty is not itself clearly within the restricted class, so whether the restriction bites is a judgement call — verify the definition against this deal. Related: waiver (spent) — One-off consent under §12.4 for the Seaside Hotels (Muscat) demand-forecasting SOW only. Excludes extensions, any other Hospitality Business and all AtliQ Affiliates.
findings.contract_quote: Partner Hotel Ranking Module — a ranking and recommendation service that scores, ranks and surfaces Partner Hotels in the United Arab Emirates and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to TravelHub users at the point of search and itinerary building, taking into account user fit, price competitiveness, partner commission tier, availability and conversion likelihood, and that drives the sort order of hotel results and "recommended stay" placements for booking through the TravelHub App;

evidence.quote: the Supplier undertakes that neither it nor any of its Affiliates shall, during the Restricted Period, directly or indirectly, provide data analytics, artificial intelligence or revenue-management services to any Hospitality Business in the GCC.
evidence.label: Signed: al noor hospitality msa §12.1 (Active until 14 Sep 2029)

evidence.quote: "Hospitality Business" means any person, firm or entity that owns, operates, manages or franchises hotels, resorts or serviced apartments, or that provides distribution, revenue-management or guest-analytics services to any such person, firm or entity.

services are provided "in the GCC" if the Hospitality Business receiving them is headquartered in, or the services relate to properties or operations located in, any state of the GCC, irrespective of where the services are performed.
The Supplier shall procure that each of its Affiliates complies with this Clause 12 as if it were a party to this Agreement, and any breach by an Affiliate shall be deemed a breach by the Supplier.
"Restricted Period" means the Term and the period of eighteen (18) months following the expiry or termination of this Agreement.

This consent is strictly limited to the Seaside SOW. findings.title: Wrong AtliQ entity: AtliQ Inc named for a UAE counterparty
findings.explanation: Per finance's entity sheet, AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd serves every non-US client and AtliQ Inc serves US clients only. The entity in the contract decides who invoices, which tax regime applies (GST vs US) and which bank account is paid — mismatches caused payment delays twice in 2025.

findings.title: Automatic acceptance after silence
findings.explanation: Clause 5.2 deems a Deliverable accepted if TravelHub does not respond within ten business days, potentially forcing AtliQ to treat non‑conforming work as accepted and limiting recourse for defects. This creates exposure to payment disputes and liability for unsatisfactory deliverables.
findings.contract_quote: TravelHub shall review each Deliverable within ten (10) business days of delivery and either confirm Acceptance or provide a written list of material non-conformities. If TravelHub fails to respond within such period, the Deliverable shall be deemed accepted.

findings.title: Invoicing entity differs from the contracting entity
findings.explanation: AtliQ Inc signs, but §7.1 has invoices raised by AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd (Indian GSTIN). The entity that invoices must be the one named in the parties clause; a mismatch is exactly what delayed payments twice in 2025.
findings.contract_quote: Invoices under this Agreement shall be raised by AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd, GSTIN 27AAKCA4821F1Z3, on or after Acceptance of each milestone as set out in Schedule B.

evidence.quote: Mismatches between the contracting entity and the invoicing entity have caused payment delays twice in 2025.

escalation_hints: Check with Finance — invoicing entity, tax regime and bank account follow the contracting entity.

findings.title: Unilateral termination for convenience
findings.explanation: TravelHub can end the agreement at any time with 30 days' notice while AtliQ cannot, creating exposure to lost revenue and sunk costs without reciprocal rights.
findings.contract_quote: TravelHub may terminate for convenience with thirty (30) days' written notice and shall pay for all work performed up to the termination date.

findings.title: Indemnity for IP infringement may exceed liability cap
findings.explanation: AtliQ must indemnify TravelHub for any third‑party IP infringement claims, but the liability cap in §12.2 does not apply to indemnity obligations, exposing AtliQ to unlimited financial risk.
findings.contract_quote: AtliQ shall defend and indemnify TravelHub against third-party claims alleging that the Deliverables infringe any intellectual property right.

findings.title: Unspecified timeframe for correcting non‑conformities
findings.explanation: Clause 5.3 requires AtliQ to correct any notified non‑conformity and re‑submit "within a reasonable time," without defining what is reasonable. This ambiguity could lead to disputes over whether AtliQ met its obligations, affecting acceptance and payment.
findings.contract_quote: AtliQ shall correct any notified non-conformity and re-submit the Deliverable within a reasonable time.

findings.title: VAT‑exclusive fee may trigger tax compliance issues
findings.explanation: Clause 6.2 states fees are exclusive of any applicable value added tax, which must be charged in addition. As the contract is with a UAE entity, AtliQ may need to register for UAE VAT and remit tax, creating a compliance and cash‑flow risk if not anticipated.
findings.contract_quote: The fees are exclusive of any applicable value added tax, which, if applicable, shall be charged in addition.

findings.title: Obligation to comply with UAE and Saudi data laws
findings.explanation: AtliQ must process personal data in line with UAE Federal Decree‑Law No.45/2021 and, where applicable, Saudi law, which may conflict with US data‑privacy obligations and increase compliance burden.
findings.contract_quote: AtliQ shall process personal data only on TravelHub's documented instructions and in compliance with Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data and, where applicable, the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law.

findings.title: UAE law and local courts
findings.explanation: AtliQ's default is Indian law for Pvt Ltd and US state law for Inc. UAE is the counterparty's home law, which AtliQ has accepted before when needed (English law for Northwind, DIFC for Al Noor, Singapore/SIAC for CloudSpan). Forum: The courts of the Emirate of Dubai (onshore Dubai Courts) shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute arising out of or in connection with this Agreement (§15.2). Disputes would be run under unfamiliar law, typically needing local counsel.
findings.contract_quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Emirate of Dubai and the applicable federal laws of the United Arab Emirates.
